# v0.8.7 validation record

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This record covers the isolated `moddotplot-interactive-0.8.7-source` copy. The sibling

## Release checks

The final local release run was completed on 2026-09-29 with Node 25.9.0, npm
11.12.1, the pinned Rust 1.98.0 toolchain, and the regenerated optimized Wasm package.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust format, lint, tests, and Wasm target | Passed: rustfmt clean; strict all-target/all-feature Clippy clean with warnings denied; 81 tests passed with 5 intentional benchmark/diagnostic ignores; all-feature `wasm32-unknown-unknown` workspace check passed |
| Indexed-transaction Wasm smoke | Passed: successful commit, explicit abort, wrong-name rejection, and multi-record rejection preserved the committed sequence set and cached memory total |
| TypeScript, production UI build, and Vitest | Passed: no-emit type check and 26-module build; 26 test files with 130 tests passed and 1 intentional scale-only skip |
| Optimized generated Wasm | Passed: v0.8.7 bindings expose `abort_fasta` and `finish_indexed_fasta`; production Wasm is 246.10 kB, 90.42 kB gzip |
| Documentation and dependency inventory | Passed: 70 Markdown documents, local links, generated parameters, and implementation contracts checked; CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM regenerated for v0.8.7 with 132 components |
| Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit application suite | Passed: 89 cases passed, 4 expected platform-specific skips, 0 failures |
| Indexed browser matrix | Passed in all three engines: plain FAI lazy load, BGZF FAI/GZI lazy load, ordinary-gzip eager fallback, orphan-index rejection, and stale-header rejection; 15/15 scenario-engine combinations passed |

The indexed append is transactional inside Wasm. Records emitted by an intermediate
FASTA chunk remain provisional until indexed finalization verifies that exactly one
record matches the FAI name and length. Read, parse, allocation, serialization,
cancellation, record-count, name, and length failures all roll back to the sequence and
memory checkpoint established before the record began.

## Human-scale ingestion benchmark

The maintained benchmark used one 101,161,492-base chromosome record in a
102,426,018-byte plain FASTA and a 31,179,430-byte BGZF representation. Chromium
151.0.7922.34 ran headlessly on an Apple M1 Pro with 32 GiB memory. Each case used one
warmup followed by three measured runs, with a fresh browser context and page for each
run. All 12 measured v0.8.7 runs completed with no page or console errors.

Median times are split between input selection and availability of **Explore**
(landing), then **Explore** through the first self-plot **Ready** state (plot):

| Input path | Landing | First plot | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| v0.8.6 eager plain baseline | 801 ms | 6,316 ms | 7,116 ms |
| v0.8.7 eager plain | 800 ms | 6,338 ms | 7,138 ms |
| v0.8.6 eager BGZF baseline | 1,306 ms | 6,325 ms | 7,635 ms |
| v0.8.7 eager BGZF | 1,304 ms | 6,795 ms | 8,124 ms |
| v0.8.7 indexed plain plus FAI | 32 ms | 7,260 ms | 7,292 ms |
| v0.8.7 indexed BGZF plus FAI/GZI | 32 ms | 7,369 ms | 7,400 ms |

Indexed metadata reached the launch screen 25.31 times faster than the v0.8.6 plain
baseline and 41.11 times faster than the v0.8.6 BGZF baseline. This single-record
fixture still has to read, validate, pack, and plot the entire selected chromosome
after **Explore**, so indexing principally moves that work out of the landing phase.
The larger practical benefit is multi-FASTA input: unselected records are never read or
packed. The eager plain result was effectively neutral. The v0.8.7 BGZF plot phase was
7.43% slower in this three-run sample, with wider current-run timing variation; this is
reported as observed rather than attributed to a specific regression.

One additional indexed run sampled post-plot resource reporting. Plain FAI input
reported **Memory ~108.5 MiB** and BGZF FAI/GZI reported **Memory ~108.4 MiB**; both
were admitted by the declared resource plan. Chromium reported 15.2 MB and 17.1 MB of
used JavaScript heap respectively. These are single-run retained operational samples,
not browser-process peak-memory measurements.

The complete methodology and run-level evidence are summarized in the
[v0.8.7 ingestion benchmark](../../benchmarks/2026-09-29-v0.8.7-ingestion.md).

## Acceptance focus

The final browser matrix covers eager plain/gzip/BGZF behavior, visible progress,
indexed metadata-first loading, on-demand resident reuse, strict FAI/GZI and real-header
validation, fallbacks, orphan indexes, cancellation, stale-publication filtering, and
deferred landing annotations. Indexed and eager records enter the same Rust FASTA
parser and packed-sequence representation before scientific calculation. Existing
v0.8.6 estimator, exact-display, grid, annotation, and export regressions remain
applicable and passed in the complete application suite.

## Remaining release-finalization scope

This workspace is an extracted source directory rather than a Git checkout. Annotated
tagging, clean-commit provenance, reproducible source/binary archive generation, and
remote release publication remain outside this local comparison build.
